mainTopic: Whether קנין פירות is like קנין הגוף: the dispute of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about reciting over בכורים during יובל, with proofs, a parallel among תנאים, and support for each side
overview: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about someone who buys land while יובל is in force, when the land must go back to the seller. Both agree he brings בכורים, but רבי יוחנן says he also recites the declaration and ריש לקיש says he does not. The root of the argument is whether owning the produce (קנין פירות) counts like owning the land itself (קנין הגוף). A צריכא explains why this argument had to be stated alongside the earlier case of a sale for produce. Two משניות seem to support רבי יוחנן. They are answered first by saying they speak of a time without יובל, and then, using רב חסדא, by saying they speak of the first יובל. The גמרא next suggests that the same question splits the תנאים in a ברייתא about a son who bought a field from his father. רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects this, saying רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון learn their rule from an extra word in the פסוק. רב יוסף shows that רבי יוחנן must hold קנין פירות כקנין הגוף, or almost no one could bring בכורים. Finally, רבא announces that a פסוק and a ברייתא support ריש לקיש, and the proofs continue on the next amud.

steps.title: The dispute about buying land while יובל is in force
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says a buyer of land during the time of יובל brings בכורים and recites the declaration. ריש לקיש says he brings but does not recite.
steps.simpleTranslation: When יובל is in force, רבי יוחנן says: the buyer brings בכורים and recites. ריש לקיש says: he brings but does not recite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, this time about anyone who buys land while the laws of יובל apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יובל is in force, every sale of land is temporary, because the field goes back to its original owner in the יובל year. So the buyer really owns only the use of the land until then. The question is whether he can honestly say the declaration of בכורים about 'the land You gave me.'

steps.title: The reasoning behind each side
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that קנין פירות is like קנין הגוף. ריש לקיש holds that it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he brings and recites because owning the produce counts like owning the land itself. ריש לקיש says he brings but does not recite because owning the produce does not count like owning the land itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the principle behind each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The declaration says 'the land that You gave me,' so the person reciting must count as an owner of the land. רבי יוחנן says that owning the produce for a time is real ownership for this purpose. ריש לקיש says it is not, so the buyer cannot truthfully say those words.

keyTerms.meaning: Ownership of the produce or use of something, not the thing itself
Ownership of the item itself
Is considered like / is comparable
Not

steps.whyThisMatters: The question of whether קנין פירות is like קנין הגוף is a major principle that comes up in many places in ש״ס, far beyond בכורים.

steps.title: Why the dispute is needed in both cases, part one
steps.stepSummary: If the argument had been stated only about a sale for produce, we might think ריש לקיש agrees with רבי יוחנן in the יובל case, because there the buyer intended to buy the land itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is necessary to state both. If it were said only in that case (a sale for produce), we would say ריש לקיש rules this way only there, because when the buyer took the field he meant to get only the produce. But in this case (יובל), where he took it meaning to get the land itself, you might say he agrees with רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a צריכא, explaining why we need to hear the same argument twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case the buyer agreed from the start to buy only the produce. In the יובל case he thought of himself as buying the land, even though it will return at יובל. So from the first case alone, we might have thought ריש לקיש admits that the יובל buyer recites.

steps.title: Why the dispute is needed in both cases, part two
steps.stepSummary: If the argument had been stated only about the יובל case, we might think רבי יוחנן agrees with ריש לקיש in the produce-sale case. So both are necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it were said only in this case (יובל), we would say רבי יוחנן rules this way only here. But in that case (a sale for produce), you might say he agrees with ריש לקיש. So it is necessary to state both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכא by showing the other direction and concludes that both cases had to be stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the יובל case the buyer meant to buy the land, so it is easier for רבי יוחנן to treat him as an owner. In the produce sale the buyer openly bought only the produce, so we might think even רבי יוחנן says he cannot recite. Each case adds something the other could not teach.

steps.title: Proof from a buyer of a tree and its land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה that says a person who buys a tree and its land brings בכורים and recites. This seems to support רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who buys a tree and its land brings בכורים and recites!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that seems to support רבי יוחנן against ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a buyer of land recites over his בכורים, and it does not mention any exception for the time of יובל. Land bought during the time of יובל goes back to the seller, so the buyer only really owns the produce. That matches רבי יוחנן and goes against ריש לקיש.

steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in בכורים: a buyer of a tree and its land brings and recites

steps.title: The משנה is talking about a time without יובל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers for ריש לקיש: the משנה is talking about a time when יובל is not practiced.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what are we dealing here? With a time when יובל is not practiced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by saying the משנה is talking about a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יובל is not practiced, the land never goes back, so the buyer owns it forever. In that case even ריש לקיש agrees he recites. So the משנה does not prove anything about our argument.

keyTerms.meaning: With what are we dealing here? (used to limit a source to a specific case)

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the משנה to a time without יובל, so it no longer touches the argument
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה includes the time of יובל, but it may be talking only about a permanent purchase

steps.title: Proof from a buyer of three trees
steps.stepSummary: Another משנה: a buyer of two trees in someone else's field brings but does not recite. This implies a buyer of three trees, who also gets the land, brings and recites.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who buys two trees in his friend's field brings but does not recite. This implies that with three trees, he brings and recites!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second proof for רבי יוחנן from a different משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two trees do not come with the land under them, so the buyer cannot recite. Three trees do come with the land, so he recites. Again, the משנה makes no exception for the time of יובל, which seems to support רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Same answer: a time without יובל

steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is talking about a time when יובל is not practiced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the second proof the same way it pushed away the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the three trees were bought when יובל is not practiced, the land is owned forever. Then even ריש לקיש agrees the buyer recites.

steps.title: A better answer using רב חסדא: first יובל versus second יובל
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא said the argument is only about the second יובל. In the first יובל, everyone agrees the buyer brings and recites, because people did not yet count on the land going back. So the משניות can be talking about the first יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And now that רב חסדא said: the argument is in the second יובל, but in the first יובל everyone agrees he brings and recites, because they did not yet rely on it. So there is no difficulty: this משנה is about the first יובל, and ריש לקיש's ruling is about the second יובל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new and simpler way to answer the two proofs, based on רב חסדא's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We no longer need to say the משניות are talking about a time with no יובל at all. During the first יובל, people did not yet really expect land to go back, so a sale felt permanent and everyone agrees the buyer recites. The משניות are about that time, and ריש לקיש's ruling is about the second יובל, when people already counted on the land returning.

steps.title: Suggesting the argument matches an argument of תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the argument is the same as an argument between תנאים, and begins quoting a ברייתא about a son who bought a field from his father, consecrated it, and then the father died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say it is like an argument of תנאים: From where do we know that one who buys a field from his father, consecrates it, and then his father dies, the field is treated for him like a שדה אחוזה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It suggests that our argument matches an older argument of תנאים and starts quoting the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a son who bought a field from his father and consecrated it, and then the father died, so the son would have inherited it anyway. The ברייתא asks how we know the field counts for him like a שדה אחוזה, an inherited field, and not a bought one. How this connects to רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש will be shown as the ברייתא continues.

steps.title: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון learn the law from the verse
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון learn from the פסוק that a field the son was going to inherit is treated like an ancestral field, even though he bought it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'If a field that he bought, which is not from his ancestral field.' This means a field that is not fit to become an ancestral field. That leaves out this field, which is fit to become an ancestral field. These are the words of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the first opinion in the ברייתא it began quoting. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון use the פסוק to show that this son's field is not treated like a regular bought field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, a bought field that someone consecrates goes back to the seller at יובל. But this son bought the field from his father, consecrated it, and then the father died. Since the son was going to inherit it anyway, it was 'fit to be' his שדה אחוזה, so the פסוק leaves it out of the bought-field rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A bought field: a field someone purchased, not one he inherited

steps.title: רבי מאיר applies the verse to a different case
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר uses the same פסוק for a son whose father died before he consecrated the field. The גמרא then notes that for רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, that case needs no פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: How do we know that if a person bought a field from his father, then his father died, and afterward he consecrated it, it counts for him like an ancestral field? The פסוק says: 'If a field that he bought, which is not from his ancestral field.' This means a field that is not an ancestral field. That leaves out this one, which is an ancestral field. But for רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, when the father died first and then he consecrated it, no פסוק is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings רבי מאיר's opinion. He reads the same פסוק as talking about a different order of events: the father died first, and only then did the son consecrate the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר needs a פסוק even when the son inherited before consecrating. That means he thinks the death did not obviously make it an inherited field. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון think that case is obvious, so for them the פסוק must be teaching the harder case from step 11.

steps.title: רבי מאיר holds that owning the produce is like owning the field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי מאיר holds קנין פירות כקנין הגוף. That is why he needs a פסוק even when the father died first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this what they argue about? רבי מאיר holds that owning the produce is like owning the field itself. So in this case, when the father dies, the son inherits nothing new. That is why, when the father died and afterward the son consecrated it, a פסוק is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the reason behind רבי מאיר's opinion. It suggests he holds that buying a field's produce is like buying the field itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the times of יובל, the son only bought the field's produce until יובל. If that already counts as full ownership, the father's death adds nothing, and the field still looks like a bought field. So רבי מאיר needs a פסוק to teach that it counts as an ancestral field. This matches the earlier אמורא opinion that a buyer is like a full owner.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (the גמרא suggesting an explanation as a proof)
Owning only the produce of a field
Owning the field itself
He inherits

steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the ברייתא back to the main argument of the סוגיא: is a buyer in the times of יובל a full owner, or does he only own the produce?

phrases.english: What, is it not about this that they disagree?
For Rabbi Meir holds:
owning the produce is like owning the item itself,
and in this case, at his father's death
he does not inherit anything at all,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִלְכָּךְ מֵת אָבִיו וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקְדִּישָׁהּ –
phrases.english: and therefore, if his father died and afterward he consecrated it,
a verse is needed;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי מאיר's opinion from step 12 in terms of קנין פירות
steps.raayaObject: That the argument over קנין פירות כקנין הגוף is already an argument between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר's need for a פסוק when the father died before the field was consecrated

steps.title: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון hold that owning the produce is not like owning the field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון hold that owning the produce is not full ownership. So the father's death gives the son the field, and their פסוק must be about the case where he consecrated it before the father died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון hold that owning the produce is not like owning the field itself. So in this case, at the father's death, the son now inherits the field. Therefore, if the father died and afterward the son consecrated it, no פסוק is needed. The פסוק is only needed for the case where he consecrated it and afterward his father died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its suggestion by explaining the other side. For רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, the son only owned the produce until his father died, and then he truly inherited the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If buying gave the son only the produce, then the father's death gives him the field itself as an inheritance. So it is obviously an ancestral field, and no פסוק is needed. That is why they use the פסוק for the harder case, where he consecrated the field before inheriting it. This matches the earlier אמורא opinion that a buyer is not a full owner.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (only at this point)
It was needed
And therefore

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר holds that owning the produce is like owning the field, so the father's death changes nothing and a פסוק is needed. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון hold that it is not, so the father's death gives the son the field and their פסוק teaches the harder case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon hold:

phrases.aramaic: קִנְיַן פֵּירוֹת לָאו כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: owning the produce is not like owning the item itself,
and in this case, at his father's death
it is now that he inherits [the field],

phrases.aramaic: וְהִלְכָּךְ מֵת אָבִיו וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקְדִּישָׁהּ –
phrases.english: and therefore, if his father died and afterward he consecrated it,
no verse is needed;
and when a verse was needed,
it was for where he consecrated it and afterward his father died,
phrases.notes: This is the case from step 11.

phrases.english: that it was needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבְרִי: קִנְיַן פֵּירוֹת לָאו כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the suggestion from step 13 by explaining the opinion of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון
steps.raayaObject: That the argument over קנין פירות כקנין הגוף is already an argument between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון's view that no פסוק is needed when the father died first

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects the link to the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון may also hold that owning the produce is like full ownership. They got their הלכה from a closer reading of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Really, I can tell you that in general רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון hold that owning the produce is just like owning the field itself. But here, they found something in the פסוק and learned from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק pushes back on the גמרא's suggestion from steps 13–14 that the תנאים argue about קנין פירות. This step also sets up the next move, where we will see exactly what they learned from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14, the גמרא said רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון think owning the produce is NOT full ownership. רב נחמן בר יצחק says no: they could agree with רבי מאיר on that point. Their different use of the פסוק comes from the wording of the פסוק, not from the קנין פירות question.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually: used to reject a suggestion and keep the original idea
Owning only the produce (the fruits or crops) of something
Owning the thing itself
They found a verse and expounded it: they learned from extra wording

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Really, I can say to you,

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָלְמָא קָסָבְרִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: in general, Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon hold
that owning the produce is like owning the thing itself.
And here, Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon
found a verse and expounded it:

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ, בְּעָלְמָא קָסָבְרִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in steps 13–14 that the תנאים argue about קנין פירות.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון hold owning the produce is not full ownership.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Their reading can come from the wording of the פסוק instead of from a view about קנין פירות.

steps.title: The extra word in the פסוק about the bought field
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק could have said simply 'which is not his ancestral field'. The extra words 'from the field of' (משדה) teach that only a field that could never become ancestral counts as a bought field.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah could have written: 'If a field he bought, which is not his ancestral field.' So why does it say 'from his ancestral field'? To teach: only a field that is not fit to become an ancestral field counts as bought. This field is left out, because it is fit to become an ancestral field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly what רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון learned from the פסוק. The extra wording includes a field the son was going to inherit, even if he set it aside to הקדש before his father died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shorter wording would have been 'אשר לא אחוזתו'. The extra word מִשְּׂדֵה ('from the field of') teaches about a field that is fit to become ancestral land. So it is treated like ancestral land, even if the father was still alive when the son set it aside. This דרשה does not depend on the קנין פירות question at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the Torah write: the Torah could have written it more simply
A field he bought
An ancestral field: land a person inherited as his family's portion
Fit / set to become

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One write:
"If a field that he bought,
which is not his ancestral field";
what is "from the field of his ancestral holding"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:22. The Torah could have just said 'his אחוזה', so the extra word משדה ('from the field of') is what they learn from.

phrases.aramaic: שָׂדֶה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה –
phrases.english: A field that is not fit to become an ancestral field;
this one is left out,
since it is fit to become an ancestral field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reading of the פסוק that step 15 promised.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון's הלכה comes from the wording of the פסוק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra word מִשְּׂדֵה in מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּתוֹ (ויקרא 27:22), which could have read just אֲחוּזָּתוֹ.
steps.whatToRemember: The argument between the תנאים does not have to be about קנין פירות. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון can learn their rule from extra wording in the פסוק.

steps.title: רב יוסף: רבי יוחנן must hold owning produce is full ownership
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says רבי יוחנן had to hold that owning the produce is like full ownership. Otherwise his ruling about brothers who split an inheritance would leave him stuck.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: If רבי יוחנן had not said that owning the produce is like owning the thing itself, he would be stuck in the study hall. Because רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: brothers who divided an inheritance are like buyers, and they give the land back to each other in יובל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף shows that רבי יוחנן needs the rule that owning the produce is like full ownership. He quotes another ruling of רבי יוחנן about brothers splitting an inheritance, and the next step explains the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says brothers who split an inheritance are treated like buyers from each other. So each brother's portion goes back in יובל, and he only really holds it until then, which is like owning only the produce. This sets up the problem with ביכורים in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He would not find his hands and feet: he would be totally stuck
Brothers who divided an inheritance
Buyers
The Jubilee year, when bought land goes back to its original owners

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
If not for the fact that Rabbi Yochanan said
that owning the produce is like owning the thing itself,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מָצָא יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ.
phrases.english: he would not find his hands and feet in the study hall.
phrases.notes: A saying: he would be stuck, because his own rulings would clash with each other.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Brothers who divided an inheritance are buyers,
and they give the land back to each other in the Jubilee year;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תנאים and turns to רבי יוחנן's own view on קנין פירות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן holds that owning the produce is like full ownership. This must be so because of his ruling that brothers who split an inheritance are buyers who give back in יובל.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier case. Here the 'buyers' are brothers who inherited together and then divided the land. They did not buy it from strangers.

steps.title: Otherwise almost no one could bring ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: If owning the produce were not full ownership, then only an only son of an only son, all the way back to יהושע בן נון, could bring ביכורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think it is not like owning the thing itself, you would never find anyone bringing ביכורים, except an only son of an only son, going all the way back to יהושע בן נון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב יוסף's proof. It shows the strange result we would get if רבי יוחנן held that owning the produce is not full ownership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any brothers who split land only hold it until יובל, so it is like owning just the produce. If that is not real ownership, they could not bring ביכורים as their own land. Only a family with one heir in every generation since the land was divided under יהושע would truly own its land. Since that is impossible to accept, רבי יוחנן must hold that owning the produce counts.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would think: introduces a claim to show it can't be right
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש, only from a person's own land
An only son of an only son

phrases.english: And if it would enter your mind
that it is not like owning the thing itself,
you would not find anyone who brings first fruits

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא חַד בַּר חַד עַד יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן!
phrases.english: except an only son of an only son, back to Joshua son of Nun!
phrases.notes: יהושע split up the land of ישראל. Only a family with one heir every generation since then never had brothers dividing it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ לָאו כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יוסף's proof by showing the absurd result.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן holds owning the produce is like full ownership.
steps.raayaSupportSource: His ruling that brothers who divided are buyers. Without the rule, almost nobody could bring ביכורים.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יוסף, רבי יוחנן's two rulings only fit together if owning the produce counts as real ownership. Otherwise almost nobody could ever bring ביכורים.

steps.title: רבא: a פסוק and a ברייתא support ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: רבא announces that a פסוק and a ברייתא both support ריש לקיש, and starts with the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A פסוק and a ברייתא both support ריש לקיש. The פסוק:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line: רבא announces two proofs for ריש לקיש, who disagrees with רבי יוחנן. The actual פסוק comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the סוגיא showed why רבי יוחנן needs the rule that owning the produce counts. Now רבא switches sides and says the sources back ריש לקיש, who disagrees with רבי יוחנן in this סוגיא. He promises two kinds of support, a פסוק and a ברייתא, and begins with the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: They support him
A teaching of the תנאים; here a ברייתא

phrases.english: Rava said:
A verse and a baraita
support Reish Lakish.
The verse:

steps.triggerLanguage: קְרָא וּמַתְנִיתָא מְסַיְּיעִי לֵיהּ לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending רבי יוחנן to bringing support for ריש לקיש.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's opinion against רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A פסוק and a ברייתא, which will be quoted next.
